headline: Conditionally approved a 16-lot subdivision on Elwood Road and adopted the FY 2028-2033 capital improvement plan.

# LONDONDERRY, NH PLANNING BOARD

## MINUTES OF THE MEETING OF OCTOBER 14, 2026

## AT THE MOOSE HILL COUNCIL CHAMBERS

Meeting Link: http://173.166.17.35/internetchannel/show/14367?channel=4

Members Present: Jake Butler, Chair; Jeff Penta, Vice Chair; Art Rugg, Secretary; Tony DeFrancesco, Assistant Secretary; John Farrell, Member; Ann Chiampa, Member; Giovanni Verani, Ex-Officio; Shawn Faber, Town Council Ex-Officio; Jason Knights, Alternate; Brent Lyskawa, Alternate

Members Absent: Jonathan Cruz, Ex-Officio; Ryan Ouellette, Alternate

Also Present: Jacob LaFontaine, Director of Planning and Economic Development; Kirsten Hildonen, Administrative Services Director; Justin Campo, Finance Director; Phil LeBlanc, Deputy Fire Chief; Dave Wholley, DPW Director; Kim Bernard, Acting Town Manager

## I. CALL TO ORDER

Chair Butler called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. and led the Pledge of Allegiance.

## II. ADMINISTRATIVE BOARD WORK

### A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

Approval of minutes was postponed until November.

### B. REGIONAL IMPACT DETERMINATION

There were no cases of regional impact.

### C. DISCUSSIONS WITH TOWN STAFF

Jacob LaFontaine introduced himself and reviewed the organizational chart for the Planning and Economic Development Department.

## III. NEW PLANS / CONCEPTUAL PLANS

### A. Public hearing on a formal request for an amendment of the conditions of approval for a proposed sewer pump station upgrade in the Industrial -I (IND-1) Zone. 12 Jack's Bridge Road, Tax Map 15, Lot 103-1, 12 Jack's Bridge LLC (applicant), Charles H. Evans (Owner).

Chair Butler read the case into the record.

**J. Farrell made a motion to accept the application as complete per the Staff Recommendation Memo. A. Rugg seconded the motion. The motion carried 8-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative.**

Laura Gandia of Devine, Millimet & Branch and Tyler Murphy of By Land LLC appeared before the Board to discuss this request to amend precedent condition #3 regarding upgrading the sewer pump station. After discussions with the property owner and Town Staff, it was agreed that a performance guarantee agreement with a cash surety and performance guarantee would be executed to complete the sewer pump station. L. Gandia reviewed the requested changes to the condition of approval.

The Board asked about the Town's liability. T. Murphy noted that it was minimal, and that the value is third-party reviewed.

The Board noted that if the Town assumes ownership of the pump station, the taxpayers would be responsible for any future problems. So, the Board needs to ensure the project is engineered appropriately. T. Murphy explained the design came from inspections done by the Town in 2022 and 2023, and recently updated by the DPW. L. Gandia said the Town can dictate the specifications, as Staff has the say on the final agreement. J. LaFontaine verified that Town counsel would need to review the agreement before it is signed; this is included in the conditions of approval.

The Board clarified that this agreement does not guarantee that the Town will take possession of the pump station. It states that the station must be acceptable to the Town when it is presented to Town Council for acceptance.

The Board noted the loss of tax revenue if this proposal is not accepted at this time, thus delaying the start of the project.

Chair Butler asked for public comment; there was none. Chair Butler closed public comment.

**J. Farrell made a motion that the precedent condition below must be met, of which the condition is that the owner shall execute and provide a performance guarantee agreement together with a cash surety and performance guarantee to complete sewer pump station work as agreed to and approved by Town Staff. J. Penta seconded the motion. The motion carried 8-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative.**

### B. Public hearing on a minor site plan amendment for an existing gas station, the intent is to facilitate improved site circulation in the Commercial-II (C-II) Zone, 178 Rockingham Road, Tax Map 15, Lot 61-0, Nouria Energy Retail, Inc. (applicant) and 2V Londonderry LLC (owner).

Chair Butler read the case into the record.

Ari Pollack of Gallagher, Callahan & Gartrell and James Robinson of TFMoran appeared before the Board to discuss minor changes proposed to improve traffic flow through the site. These are private improvements on a private site. A. Pollack described the changes, explaining that Staff suggested they should be presented to the Board instead of working at the administrative level. The Board agreed these changes would make it safer and easier to navigate the site.

The Board noted there is little difficulty in turning left from the site. They suggested removing the median instead of flattening it, and A. Pollack agreed. The Board also asked that "Do not block" be repainted on Symmes Drive. A. Pollack agreed, if the Town grants permission. Chair Butler asked the DPW to work with the applicant on this.

Chair Butler asked for public comment; there was none. Chair Butler closed public comment.

**A. Rugg made a motion to accept the application as complete. T. DeFrancesco seconded the motion. The motion carried 8-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative.**

**J. Farrell made a motion to accept the minor site plan amendment, with the applicant making a change to the site layout to remove the median and allow left-hand turns, and that DPW will make any decisions at their preconstruction meeting on painting and location placement of the "Do not block" on Symmes Drive. A. Rugg seconded the motion. The motion carried 8-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative.**

### C. Public hearing on a formal application of a subdivision for 16 residential lots and associated site improvements in the Agricultural Residential (AR-I) District. 35 Elwood Road, Map 5 Lot 39; 16 Dan Hill Road, Map 5 Lot 39-5; 54A Elwood Road, Map 5 Lot 40; 68 Rear Elwood Road, and Map 5 Lot 72, Estate of Wayne Elwood c/o Linda & Christina Elwood (owner) & Belize Real Estate Holdings, LLC (applicant).

Chair Butler read the case into the record.

G. Verani recused himself from this hearing.

**J. Farrell made a motion to accept the application as complete for acceptances purposes only, and any outstanding checklist items will become conditions of approval. A. Rugg seconded the motion. The motion carried 7-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative.**

J. Penta recused himself from this hearing. Chair Butler appointed J. Knights to sit in for J. Penta.

J. LaFontaine noted there is a stormwater basin shown within the utility easement. The applicant has met with the utility company, who they believe is willing to exercise an easement. If not, they discussed relocating the basin or using infiltration to handle runoff. The owner of Lot 40-15 will be responsible for the maintenance of the basin, if it is located on their property. There is also a driveway curb cut located in the utility easement.

Jacob Doerfler of The Dubay Group appeared before the Board to discuss this request to create a 16-lot subdivision. J. Doerfler described the project and proposed improvements.

J. LaFontaine noted the Conservation Commission requested a no-cut zone at the existing tree line and a buffer along the north side of the stream. J. Doerfler said buffer signs are along the 50-foot wetland buffer; they are open to expanding that to a portion along the tree line. He asked that the buffer signs be directed along the property line instead of the tree line at Lots 39-12, 39-13, and 39-14 to avoid encumbering those lots.

A. Rugg reported the applicant met with the Heritage Commission, noting that the existing structures did not appear to be salvageable. They asked to conduct a site walk; however, the property owner said it would not be safe to enter the buildings. The Commission asked to preserve as many apple trees as possible and to use the stones from any stone walls for decorative purposes.

Chair Butler asked for public comment.

**Graham Nadig, 13 Dan Hill Road,** said the former property owner kept the pond on Dan Hill Road clear. If the outflow is blocked, it will flood over the road. J. Doerfler said no drainage would be directed that way.

**Thomas Agrella, 46 Elwood Road,** said the farm has an easement to his property for the power lines. J. Doerfler said they will not be impacting this area.

Chair Butler closed public comment.

**J. Farrell made a motion to accept the waiver from LSR 4.10 relating to plan scale as it can be granted without substantial detriment to the public good. J. Knights seconded the motion. The motion carried 7-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative.**

**J. Farrell made a motion to grant conditional approval of a subdivision for 35 and 54A Elwood Road, 68 Rear Elwood Road, 16 Dan Hill Road, Map 5 Lots 39, 40, 72, 39-5, Zoned AR-1, Estate of Wayne Elwood c/o Linda & Christina Elwood (owner) & Belize Real Estate Holdings, LLC (applicant), in accordance with the plans prepared by The Dubay Group dated December 12, 2025, last revised September 11, 2026. A. Rugg seconded the motion. The motion carried 7-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative.**

G. Verani and J. Penta returned to the Board.

## IV. OLD BUSINESS

### A. Formal application of a site plan for sixty (60) residential units, with associated site improvements along with a Conditional Use Permit for 597 Square feet of wetland buffer impact, in the Commercial II (C-II) Zone and the Route 28 Performance Overlay District, 196 & 198 Rockingham Road, Tax Map 15, Lot 66 & 66 -1, S&S Metal Recycling, Inc (Owner) and Gino Bernard (Applicant). (Continued from 6/3 and 8/5, has requested a continuance to 11/4/2026)

S. Faber stepped away from the Board.

**A. Rugg made a motion to continue this case to November 4, 2026. J. Knights seconded the motion. The motion carried 7-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative.**

S. Faber returned to the Board.

## V. OTHER BUSINESS

### A. Public Hearing for the adoption of the FY 2028-2033 Capital Improvement Plan (CIP). The proposed plan can be viewed during business hours in the Planning & Economic Development Department.

K. Hildonen presented the final summary of all capital projects presented to the CIP Committee. The Board discussed whether the CIP was a wish list or a plan for needed improvements.

J. Penta, CIP Committee member, explained that in an effort to be more transparent, projects were presented that were not only capital improvements projects, but also routine operational costs and items covered by warrant article. He noted the intent was to balance the impact of capital expenditures on the tax rate over a number of years.

J. Campo explained how this CIP differs from those in the past. The intent was to use it as a planning tool so that large expenditures could be scheduled to avoid spikes in specific years.

K. Hildonen reviewed items highlighted by the CIP Committee as most significant, noting that they used the process to prioritize projects. The Board discussed the definition of a capital improvement project, and which items on the current CIP qualified as such.

Deputy Fire Chief Phil LeBlanc noted that capital reserve funds are a funding mechanism for capital improvements. By definition, a capital improvement is equipment, facilities, and infrastructure. They were asked to add the vehicles, as they are a large expense that needs to be planned for.

DPW Director Wholley clarified that items were added to the CIP based on the cost being over the $100,000 threshold. He noted that through the capital reserve mechanism, they have funding for some of the items. He reiterated that items are placed on the CIP because they need to be identified as occurring in the coming years.

K. Hildonen noted that capital improvement is defined in the charter, and read the definition.

After an extended discussion, the Board identified a number of items that they felt qualified as capital improvements projects. Those included a combination of specific facility repairs to the Fire Station, Leach Library Children's Room addition, DPW facility, High School addition and renovation, and turf field and turf project grouped together. The Board asked K. Hildonen to list these projects in the format used in the past, with the additional information from the CIP serving as backup.

**J. Penta made a motion to adopt as amended the current CIP plan as discussed at the 10-14-26 Planning Board meeting. J. Farrell seconded the motion. The motion carried 6-1-1, with G. Verani abstaining and J. Butler voting in the negative. Chair votes in opposition.**

The Board noted the need to avoid this situation in the future and recommended tasking J. LaFontaine with offering suggestions for improvements in the CIP process.

## VI. ADJOURNMENT

**T. DeFrancesco made a motion to adjourn the meeting. A. Rugg seconded the motion. The motion carried 8-0-0.**

The meeting was adjourned at 9:21 p.m.

These minutes were prepared by Beth Hanggeli.
